question: How are heavy and superheavy nuclei formed?
intro: My research develops computational models of heavy-ion reactions to understand and predict the formation of heavy and superheavy nuclei. Stochastic simulation, uncertainty quantification and scientific computing provide the principal methods for this work.

areas.title: Nuclear Reaction Dynamics
areas.text: Langevin-based stochastic modelling of heavy-ion reactions. Fusion–evaporation reactions and the synthesis of superheavy elements are applications of the same description, with predictions for Z = 119 and Z = 120 made with KEWPIE3.

areas.title: Uncertainty Quantification
areas.text: Bayesian optimisation and machine learning applied to estimate nuclear model parameters and their uncertainties, with systematic benchmarking of competing models.

current.title: KEWPIE3 development and validation
paragraphs: **Objective:** validate and publish KEWPIE3, the refinement of the KEWPIE2 cascade code (which describes the survival of the excited nucleus) with an implemented and calibrated formation step, for fusion-evaporation cross-section predictions in superheavy element synthesis.
**Key question:** how can the calculation of the compound nucleus formation probability be improved with Langevin-based stochastic approaches?

current.title: Fusion dynamics and fusion-by-diffusion
paragraphs: **Objective:** revisit the fusion dynamics in the fusion-by-diffusion model for fusion-evaporation production cross sections.

current.title: Uncertainty analysis of nuclear reaction models
paragraphs: **Objective:** constrain the compound nucleus formation probability in superheavy element synthesis through systematic uncertainty analysis.

previous.title: Reaction mechanisms for superheavy element synthesis
paragraphs: PhD thesis, University of Caen Normandy (2024).

The thesis investigates the synthesis of superheavy elements (Z ≥ 104) by fusion–evaporation reactions, modelled in three stages: capture, formation and survival. It improves the predictive power of the Kewpie2 code by extending it with a formation step, the basis of KEWPIE3, using both overdamped and full Langevin formalisms.

The injection-point distance is optimised on cold and hot fusion data, and hot-fusion evaporation residue cross sections are reproduced to better than an order of magnitude. For cold fusion, the 1n channel deviates by a factor, while the 2n and 3n channels are within an order of magnitude. The reduced friction coefficients show that the dynamics is not fully damped, so a full one-dimensional Langevin formalism is implemented. Predictions for Z = 119 and 120 align with other codes, and a method is proposed to study formation probability ratios for ^258^No and ^259^Db.

previous.title: Even-even argon isotopes
paragraphs: Collective and mean-field models within the symmetry-conserving configuration mixing framework, with T. R. Rodríguez Frutos. Preprint on HAL.

previous.title: Master's and BSc theses
paragraphs: **MSc dissertation:** Nuclear structure studies with symmetry conserving configuration mixing methods, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Nuclear Physics (September 2020), supervised by Dr. Tomás Raúl Rodríguez Frutos.

It describes the framework of the symmetry conserving configuration mixing (SCCM) method and applies it to the even-even argon isotopes (A = 32 to 58), where the magic numbers N = 20 and 28 persist and neutron sub-shell closures appear at ^56^Ar and ^58^Ar, with binding energy per nucleon and charge radii compared with experiment. It also studies ^152,154^Nd (well deformed, with coexisting prolate and oblate rotational bands) and ^78^Kr (oblate–prolate admixture, with the moment of inertia of the first excited 0^+^ state about one third of the ground state's).
**BSc thesis:** a safety evaluation of the Ghana Research Reactor-1, University of Ghana. See [Publications](publications.html).

publications_text: Journal articles, preprints, theses, conference contributions and manuscripts in preparation are listed on the Publications page. The research software KEWPIE3, a refinement of the KEWPIE2 cascade code, is described on the [Projects](projects.html) page.
